strategies.overview: Copperajah stands out from the other Steel-types for being a defensive tank that packs both firepower and utility. It checks special wallbreakers like Diancie, Munkidori, and Porygon-Z. Additionally, Copperajah's deep movepool gives it a lot of utility options. For example, Knock Off allows it to hit item-reliant Pokemon that commonly switch into it like Rotom-H and Incineroar, letting Copperajah's entry hazards chip away at them, and Whirlwind lets it phaze setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Uxie and Porygon-Z. However, Copperajah's biggest problem is the lack of reliable recovery, making it a lot harder to consistently switch into special wallbreakers that have STAB attacks that it doesn't resist like Inteleon and Toxtricity. Copperajah also struggles to break through physical walls like Vileplume, Vaporeon, and Milotic, as they can tank its attacks and threaten it back with status.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

An Assault Vest set with an EV spread of 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe and an Adamant nature lets Copperajah outspeed foes like Registeel and Dragalge, tank hits from Porygon-Z and Kilowattrel, and be a menacing wallbreaker. Play Rough hits Fighting- and Dark-types like Mienshao, Breloom, and Wo-Chien, but it's rarely used. Supercell Slam targets bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Tentacruel. However, Copperajah struggles to fit it, and Supercell Slam's risk of recoil damage makes it very niche. Tera Water lets Copperajah better handle Ground- and Water-types like Flygon and Inteleon, but Tera Dragon is preferred for not giving it a weakness to Grass- and Electric-type attacks from Breloom and Kilowattrel. Tera Ghost gives Copperajah a useful immunity to Fighting-type attacks from foes like Mienshao and Toxicroak while spinblocking Tsareena and Brambleghast. However, these Pokemon usually can then proceed to hit it with super effective attacks like Knock Off and Poltergeist.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Mienshao, Toxicroak, Heracross, and Breloom destroy Copperajah with their STAB Close Combat, but none of them want to switch directly into its STAB attacks. Paldean Tauros-W resists Copperajah's STAB attacks, allowing it to either destroy Copperajah with its STAB Close Combat or force Copperajah to switch, giving it a free opportunity to use Bulk Up.

Physical Walls: Vileplume, Vaporeon, and Milotic can tank Copperajah's attacks very well and threaten it back with status. Orthworm is notable for also taking Copperajah's attacks very well and either using it to set up entry hazards or hitting it back with Body Press.

Ground-types: Flygon, Swampert, and Gligar can KO Copperajah with their STAB Earthquake, but they don't enjoy switching into its Knock Off, and Flygon takes a lot of damage from its Iron Head.

Fire-types: Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion can put a lot of pressure on Copperajah with their STAB attacks, but they have to be cautious about switching into its Knock Off. Incineroar can force Copperajah to switch out, allowing it to freely set up with Swords Dance, or destroy Copperajah with its STAB Flare Blitz. Rotom-H can use Copperajah as setup fodder or cripple it heavily with Pain Split. However, Rotom-H doesn’t enjoy directly switching into its Knock Off.

movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Set Details

Knock Off allows Copperajah to target item-reliant foes like Rotom-H, Kilowattrel, and Incineroar. For its last move, Copperajah commonly runs Whirlwind, allowing it to phaze bulky setup sweepers like Calm Mind Cresselia and Sylveon. Alternatively, Protect allows Copperajah to scout out Choice item attackers like Flygon, Mienshao, and Munkidori and gives it more Leftovers recovery. Earthquake hits Fire- and Poison-types like Chandelure and Galarian Slowbro and Steel-types like Registeel, Klefki, and opposing Copperajah. The Speed investment allows Copperajah to outpace Bronzong. Tera Dragon gives Copperajah a useful resistance to Fire-type attacks from foes like Chandelure and Rotom-H, while Tera Fairy gives it a better matchup against Flygon and Fighting-types like Mienshao and Breloom.

Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon provide massive recovery for Copperajah, letting it repeatedly switch into foes like Munkidori and Porygon-Z. Copperajah best synergizes with physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Vileplume, and Vaporeon, as they can handle physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak, Paldean Tauros-W, and Basculegion-M. In return, Copperajah checks special wallbreakers like Munkidori, Kilowattrel, and Dragalge. Copperajah is forced out by Fire-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, as they can destroy it with their Fire-type attacks. Thus, it pairs well with Water- and Dragon-types like Vaporeon, Dragalge, and Goodra to check them. Copperajah appreciates Fairy- and Psychic-types like Sylveon, Cresselia, and Diancie, as they can handle foes like Heracross, Flygon, and Incineroar. Wallbreakers such as Flygon, Overqwil, and Paldean Tauros-W appreciate Copperajah's strength, since unlike other Steel-types such as Bronzong, Klefki, and Registeel, it can wear down physical walls like Gligar, Galarian Slowbro, and Swampert.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 2-3 points

Overview: Copperajah is a budget wallbreaker with solid Attack, good STAB moves, excellent coverage, and enough utility to fit on teams that still need to bolster their defensive profile with a Steel-type late into a draft. On the other hand, it has low defenses without significant investment, no access to reliable recovery, an irredeemable Speed stat, and less tools and utility than the average Steel-type brings to the table, hence the lower price.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Copperajah's toolkit best contributes to spreading damage on the opposing team, with Sheer Force or Heavy Metal alongside a damage-boosting item to increase the power of both its STAB attacks and coverage. Copperajah can make switching in on it difficult due to the amount of strong moves it has access to, being able to run more flexible coverage than similarly priced options. Rarely, it can also set up with Curse, further strengthening itself while being harder to knock out in return.

Offensive Utility: If Copperajah is needed to fill another role, it can act as a defensive switch-in to special attackers with Assault Vest alongside Special Defense investment or as utility with Knock Off, Stealth Rock, and Whirlwind to force foes out of position.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Heavy Slam, Iron Head

Setup Moves: Curse

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Knock Off, Whirlwind, Taunt, Substitute, Rest, Sleep Talk, Brick Break

Coverage: Heat Crash, Play Rough, Earthquake, Superpower, Supercell Slam, Stone Edge, Rock Slide, Rock Blast, Zen Headbutt, Outrage

Niche Moves

Iron Defense + Body Press: While Copperajah has relatively low base Defense, and Body Press is not boosted by STAB or Sheer Force, it can utilize IronPress in tandem with RestTalk, a Chesto Berry, or additional coverage to have strong Fighting-type coverage while being nearly impossible to KO with physical attacks alongside its other standard tools.

Bulldoze / Rock Tomb: While Copperajah is almost never outspeeding its foes, it can lower the foe's Speed at the cost of Base Power for its teammates to take advantage later in the battle as long as it doesn't negate these secondary effects with Sheer Force.

Common Items

Life Orb: Life Orb loses its drawbacks when paired with Sheer Force while significantly boosting the power of many moves Copperajah normally carries, like Iron Head and Play Rough.

Assault Vest: Copperajah's wide coverage and high HP stat make it a decent Assault Vest user to shut down opposing special attackers that lack strong coverage, letting it switch in and heavily pressure foes in return while taking minimal damage.

Choice Band: Copperajah can further boost its immediate damage with all moves via Choice Band, restricting its ability to switch moves but making it very difficult for even foes that resist its attacks to switch in.

Niche Items

Leftovers: Specifically on Curse and Iron Defense sets, Leftovers can provide more recovery to Copperajah than other items would while not forcing it to use up a moveslot with Rest, keeping it healthy while it sets up.

Resistance Berries: Against frail foes with strong coverage against Copperajah, it can use an Occa, Chople, or Shuca Berry to survive a strong attack that it normally wouldn't be able to and damage or even KO the foe in return.

Eject Pack: Copperajah can use Eject Pack alongside Superpower to deal damage and gain momentum as a pivot a single time while also avoiding being stuck on the field with reduced stats.

Chesto Berry: Copperajah can heal any damage or status it takes during battle a single time using Rest paired with a Chesto Berry, allowing it to further pressure the opposing team that might've expected any chip damage to be permanent.

Tera

One of Copperajah's best traits is its Steel typing, so being a Tera Captain would only be useful if the team had no better options. If it is the only lower-tier option, it can run Tera Water to maintain a strong defensive profile, Tera Fairy to do the same while empowering Play Rough, or Tera Steel to further strengthen its STAB attacks. Defensively, Tera Fire, Grass, Ghost, and Flying can all flip some of its weaknesses in specific matchups.

Draft Strategy

Copperajah provides a Steel-type's defensive profile and a decent offensive profile for people who are lacking in both late in the draft with relatively few points. It is never the star player on a team, and teams will want to consider having solid alternative checks to foes that Steel-types normally deal with.

Checks and Counters

Super Effective Attacks: Copperajah's low Speed and questionable defenses mean any super effective damage taken from foes stacks up quickly, making it tricky to switch Copperajah in on foes that may be carrying coverage for it. Foes like Urshifu-R, Volcarona, and Landorus-T threaten it with strong STAB moves that they're likely already bringing to the battle regardless.

Chip Damage: Copperajah's lack of reliable recovery and reliance on offensive items mean any damage it takes is relatively permanent, especially if it uses Life Orb alongside moves without secondary effects or without Sheer Force.

Defensive Foes: Against foes that resist its STAB moves, have recovery options, and aren't too bothered by its coverage, Copperajah can have trouble making a meaningful impact on battles.
